messages:
maria_ops: FYI customer 'BrightLeaf' just opened a P1 — they see intermittent 5xx + long tail timeouts on hosted inference. Happening ~13:12 UTC, ~30% of requests hitting 504 / 5xx. Sharing logs and trace IDs.
support_john: Ack — opening escalation ticket. Which infra cluster/region? customer provided a curl sample and request-id headers.
aj_engineer: Looking now. Correlating with ingress metrics — we see a sharp rise in per-tenant queued requests and continuous-batcher backlog. queue_depth metric for tenant `brightleaf-prod` hit 1024 (max) ~13:11:40.
srebot: Alert: tenant_queue_depth=1024 for tenant=brightleaf-prod @ 2026-02-18T13:11:42Z, p95_dequeue_time increased from 40ms -> 1.2s, error_rate 5xx up to 28% (13:12:00 UTC).
maria_ops: Paste of customer error snippet:
```
Response: 504 Gateway Timeout
x-request-id: br-req-20260218-7a9f
error: request timed out waiting for batch slot
```
aj_engineer: Repro steps customer used:
1) ~30 concurrent streaming requests with long contexts (~2k tokens) hitting /v1/chat/stream
2) No per-request client-side retries, sustained for ~2m
3) Requests route to a single host pool because of tenant affinity and limited thinpool capacity
kelsey_se: Sounds like continuous batching is accumulating KV cache / long-seq requests and preventing new requests from entering batches. When the queue hits depth limit we early-drop or return 504s. Any change in model (longer seq) recently for this tenant?
support_john: Customer says they recently switched to the new Llama-extended model (longer context) a day ago. Traffic pattern increased after marketing campaign.
aj_engineer: Quick triage notes:
- Ingress queue backed up: `ingress.request_queue_depth{tenant=\"brightleaf-prod\"}` peaked at 1024
- Dequeue throughput dropped due to large batch assembly times and KV-cache inflation
- Early-drop policy kicked in at threshold `queue_depth>=1024` -> 5xx routing
- No autoscale triggered because dedicated thinpool is capped
Possible mitigations: bump tenant queue depth, enable burst pool, reduce max batch assemble window, or route tenant to fallback smaller model.
maria_ops: Customer asks for immediate mitigation options they can accept.
kelsey_se: Recommended immediate steps:
- Temporary: increase tenant request depth to 2048 and enable burst capacity for their dedicated pool (low-risk, buys time). `kubectl set env deploy/ingress -n hosted INGRESS_MAX_DEPTH=2048 --dry-run=client -o yaml` (ops to apply)
- Medium: set `batch.max_assemble_time_ms` to 50 from 200 for that pool to prefer lower-latency smaller batches.
- Longer: advise customer to fallback to shorter-context model variant or use streaming with smaller chunk sizes.
srebot: Note: if we increase queue depth without expanding dequeue capacity, tail-latency p99 could increase. Recommend also enabling `tenant_eviction_early_threshold=0.85` to shed aggressive tenants before full depth.
aj_engineer: Trying a quick canary: will flip `batch.max_assemble_time_ms` 200->60 on one host in the pool. Deploying now.
deploybot: deploy started: canary apply to hosted-ingress-cluster-a host-7. change set: batch.max_assemble_time_ms=60. rollout id: r-20260218-001
kelsey_se: Also prepping a script customers can run to reproduce (short curl):
```
for i in {1..40}; do
  curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"X-Client-Request-Id: br-test-$i\" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream &
done
```
support_john: I sent the customer a single-line mitigation offer: temporary burst enable + reduced batch assemble window. They accepted the temporary changes.
aj_engineer: Canary results: host-7 p95_dequeue_time down from 1.2s -> 90ms within 30s, error_rate from 28% -> 4% on canary. Proceeding to roll 20% of pool.
deploybot: rollout 20% complete -> 5 hosts updated. next checkpoint in 60s.
maria_ops: Customer reports errors dropping and requests returning. Marking incident as 'mitigated' while we continue postmortem.
aj_engineer: Postmortem action items:
- Investigate autoscale trigger thresholds for dedicated thinpools (doesn't fire when KV cache heavy)
- Add tenant-level heuristic: prefer route-to-fallback-model when long-seq spike detected
- Improve observability: surface `kvcache.size` per-tenant in console and set alert on kvcache-induced dequeue slowdowns
- Re-evaluate default `queue_depth` and early-eviction thresholds for hosted tiers
kelsey_se: I'll draft a customer-facing summary + recommended model config guidance.
srebot: Incident closed -> mitigated at 2026-02-18T13:13:05Z. Please attach traces and the rollout ids to the ticket for audit.
maria_ops: Thanks team :heart: — will follow up with PM/infra for the autoscale followup and customer RCA.
